$comment: GATING. Permanent ratification of the supersession-label exemption for frozen, digest-pinned historical records. Also serves as the exemption registry. Changes no identity, threshold, grid or prompt artifact.

the_problem.gate_as_built: Every reference to a superseded identity commit must carry an inline supersedes / lineage / RETRACTED label.
the_problem.what_it_cannot_distinguish: A STALE LIVE document that still points at an old version, from a CORRECTLY FROZEN DATED record that pointed at the then-current version and has not been touched since.
the_problem.the_circularity: oi3_release_weight_resolution.json references identity v1.2.0 because v1.2.0 was current when it was written. Identity v1.3.0 pins that record by commit AND sha256 in supplemental_records. Adding an inline label would change the record's bytes, which would falsify a pin inside the authoritative identity artifact. The gate demands an edit that breaks the authority.
the_problem.why_it_recurs: Every frozen digest-pinned historical record trips this gate again each time the identity version advances. Left unratified it is a permanent false positive that trains people to wave the gate through.

RATIFIED_TEST.statement: A reference to a superseded identity version is EXEMPT from the inline-label requirement iff ALL of the following hold.

conditions.condition: The referencing record is pinned by BOTH commit and sha256 in the superseding identity artifact's supplemental_records.
conditions.does: Establishes that the CURRENT AUTHORITY has adopted this historical record. Without it, any old document referencing an old version would be exempt merely for being old.

conditions.condition: The referencing record's last-touching commit is a STRICT ANCESTOR of the superseding identity artifact's last-touching commit.
conditions.does: Establishes the record is genuinely DATED -- it existed before the supersession and has not been edited since. Without it, a document edited today could still reference the old version and inherit exemption from a pin that was updated to match.

conditions.condition: AMENDMENT 1 -- the pin must VERIFY, not merely be present. The sha256 recorded in supplemental_records must equal the digest recomputed from the record's bytes at the pinned commit.
conditions.does: Prevents a self-certifying exemption. A gate that checks only that the fields EXIST would accept a pin naming any digest at all. This is the same defect class as an ATTESTED provenance block whose evidence refs are never resolved: shape is not attestation.

conditions.condition: AMENDMENT 2 -- the record has an entry in exemption_registry below, naming which superseded version it references and why it is exempt.
conditions.does: Relocates the DISCLOSURE rather than deleting it. See amendment_2_rationale.

RATIFIED_TEST.conjunction: ALL FOUR REQUIRED. C1 and C2 do independent work and neither implies the other.

amendment_1_rationale.coordinator_wording: 'pinned by commit AND sha in the current identity's supplemental_records'
amendment_1_rationale.gap: Ambiguous between 'the fields are present' and 'the pin resolves'. An implementation reading it the first way makes the exemption self-certifying: a stale record could carry a pin naming a digest nobody ever checks.
amendment_1_rationale.fix: The pin must resolve and match. Recompute; do not read the declared value.

amendment_2_rationale.the_cost_the_exemption_would_otherwise_i: The gate exists so a reader is never misled about which version a document depends on. Exempting the inline label removes that signal: someone opening the OI-3 record sees a reference to v1.2.0 with nothing indicating it is superseded.
amendment_2_rationale.the_resolution: THE LABEL MOVES TO A SURFACE THAT CAN LEGALLY BE EDITED. The frozen record cannot be touched without breaking its pin; the registry in this artifact can be. Disclosure is preserved, relocated rather than dropped.
amendment_2_rationale.why_not_put_it_in_the_identity_artifact: The natural home would be the supplemental_records entry itself. But editing scientific_config_identity.json changes its digest, which is embedded in the binding protocol, generation_settings, qwen_config_identity, the dose grid and the mixed-operation ruling -- a five-artifact cascade for a documentation line, days from the deadline. The registry achieves the same disclosure at zero cascade.
amendment_2_rationale.discoverability: One greppable location answers 'why does this frozen record reference a superseded version'.

no_transitivity.rule: Exemption is PER RECORD and is not inherited. A document that references an exempt record does NOT thereby become exempt; it must satisfy C1-C4 on its own.
no_transitivity.why: Otherwise an exemption chain forms and the gate's coverage decays from the leaves inward.

self_maintaining.rule: The test reads the CURRENT identity artifact. If a future identity version drops a record from supplemental_records, C1 fails and the gate correctly fires again.
self_maintaining.assessment: This is desirable, not a defect. If the current authority no longer vouches for a record, that record IS stale and should be flagged.

scope.applies_to: References to superseded versions of the identity artifact chain.
scope.does_not_apply_to: References to superseded versions of any other artifact, and any reference in a live, editable document.
scope.extension: If another chain develops the same pin-and-freeze pattern, it may request the same treatment by ruling. It is not inherited by analogy.

clarifications.gate_error_message: When the gate fires on a record that LOOKS exempt but fails one condition, the message must name WHICH condition failed. 'Missing supersession label' would send someone to edit a frozen file, which is the wrong action in three of the four failure modes.

exemption_registry.$comment: The disclosure surface. One entry per exempt record. Verified at ratification, not asserted.

entries.why_the_reference_is_correct: The record was written when v1.2.0 was current and correctly cites it. Its finding -- OI-3 verdict DIFFERENT -- is unaffected by the v1.2.0 to v1.3.0 change, which only supplied the PRIMARY params hash and closed the open items. No configuration, eligibility rule or threshold moved.
entries.C3_verification_note: Recomputed digest of the record's bytes equals the pinned sha256.

unchanged: The supersession gate itself, for every record that does not satisfy C1-C4.
scientific_config_identity.json v1.3.0 and every artifact whose digest references it.
oi3_release_weight_resolution.json -- NOT EDITED, which is the point.
Every threshold, grid, identity and prompt artifact.
hard_stops: Granting exemption on fewer than all four conditions.
Accepting a pin whose sha256 is present but not recomputed and matched.
Editing a frozen record to satisfy the gate when it qualifies for exemption -- that falsifies the pin in the authoritative artifact.
Inheriting exemption transitively through a reference to an exempt record.
A gate error that says 'missing supersession label' without naming which condition failed.
